newsitem.title: UK: UK's Finsbury AM launches first quoted hedge fund.
newsitem.headline: UK's Finsbury AM launches first quoted hedge fund.

text.p: Finsbury Asset Management Ltd is to launch a closed-end investment company focusing on hedge funds next month, the first time such a vehicle will be listed on the London Stock Exchange.

The placing of the Finsbury International Hedge Investment Company Ltd will be conducted jointly by investment banks Rea Brothers and SBC Warburg. Some 10 million ordinary shares will be offered at $10/share. Minimum investment will be $10,000.

The fund, managed by Rea Brothers (Guernsey) Investment Management Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Rea Brothers Group, will invest mainly in a diversified portfolio of 15-30 international hedge funds "aiming to achieve superior returns with low volatility".
Specialist hedge fund firm International Asset Management Ltd, regulated by IMRO and with some $500 million under management, will be the investment manager.
Rea Brothers said the manager's approach was both quantitative and qualitative and it monitors over 200 managers.

The fund will not invest directly in currencies or commodities, although it may invest in a fund which has exposure to these markets. Investment in any one fund will be limited to 10 percent of the portfolio.

"Many investors perceive global stock markets to be nearing their all-time highs and against this background the investment manager believes a company with a diversified portfolio may be an appropriate investment opportunity," said a statement from Finsbury Asset Management.
"Two major life assurance companies have already indicated their intention to invest in the fund."
Finsbury said the new hedge fund was unusual in that such vehicles usually did not undertake direct marketing and disposals at short notice were normally difficult.
Investors will enter the fund in dollars but the price will be quoted in sterling and SBC Warburg will market a market in sterling.
